security.threat: An arbitrary valid self-signature is mistaken for an independently pinned writer.
security.control: Exact independently accepted key/name/head; strict successor CAS and revocation gates.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A hashed but impossible state is accepted as computation.
security.control: Replay exact program/input/execution identity before accepting or resuming.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A mesh topic or relay is mistaken for private storage.
security.control: Separate public signaling and payload-relay consent; explicit disclosure and no privacy claim.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: An unknown DNS write is repeated after restart or key rotation.
security.control: Strict write-ahead intent and exact read-only reconciliation; unknown journal retention.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A holder supplies modified, duplicate-index or wrong-manifest bytes.
security.control: Full domain-separated commitments and exact compatible indexed recovery.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Guest output is mistaken for trusted execution or broad host authority.
security.control: Separate VM effects, bounded mounts and explicit lifecycle/command reconciliation.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Malicious same-origin code can use retained key handles and read local data.
security.control: Source/asset inventory and origin boundary; nonextractability is not protection from active same-origin code.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Untrusted messages, replay or unknown effects exhaust application allowances.
security.control: Reserve each independent resource before effects; unknown outcomes stay charged.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A relay replays or substitutes SDP/ICE and stale session callbacks.
security.control: Signed exact signaling, session/generation fencing and bounded channel flow.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Tab loss or eviction removes the only object fragments or recent trust anchor.
security.control: Explicit recovery export and origin-storage evidence; no guarantee after total information loss.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Loaded emulator, BIOS or guest differs from reviewed inventory.
security.control: Retained corresponding-source materials and exact local asset digests; live load-time remote integrity remains an assumption.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

persistence.restore: Startup restores only a valid active existing record.
persistence.trust: Missing, malformed or revoked records never authorize automatic replacement.
persistence.failure: Origin eviction or device loss can destroy the only key.

persistence.storage: Origin IndexedDB exact name/key/digest with history
persistence.restore: Admitted successors persist by exact CAS before the live head changes; live restore is explicit.
persistence.trust: Independent exact key and recent digest acceptance is not derived from a self-signature.
persistence.failure: Storage failure preserves the previous live head; total loss requires independent recent evidence.

persistence.restore: Load the exact scoped candidate and perform read-only reconciliation.
persistence.trust: No timer takeover, blind retry or deletion of unresolved intent.
persistence.failure: An absent provider read does not prove the old mutation never occurred.

persistence.storage: Session RAM plus conditionally reachable peer fragments
persistence.restore: Automatically verify received bytes; repair only within admitted budgets and checked receipts.
persistence.trust: Different peer IDs do not prove failure-domain independence or future retention.
persistence.failure: All-byte loss cannot be repaired; local storage persistence does not make object cache durable.

persistence.storage: Session state or explicitly exported recovery bundle
persistence.restore: Every received checkpoint is replayed against its exact program/input/execution identity.
persistence.trust: Replay does not grant exclusive execution or prove arbitrary guest effects.
persistence.failure: Older execution identities are refused without explicit revalidation.

persistence.storage: Session-only checked vault and user-saved external file
persistence.restore: Verify complete bundle atomically; export strips accepted-trust status.
persistence.trust: Imported keys and anchors are supplied evidence, not trusted authority.
persistence.failure: External export is not a durability certificate; stale/conflicting imports refuse.

persistence.storage: Session-local epochs plus explicit history export
persistence.restore: Unknown effects remain charged; renewal is a deliberate new allowance.
persistence.trust: No automatic refund or epoch rollover.
persistence.failure: Browser reload is not durable preservation of the budget ledger.

persistence.storage: Retained host command handles and observed lifecycle
persistence.restore: Observe the selected old command result without dispatching it again.
persistence.trust: A timeout is an unknown outcome, not cancellation or rollback.
persistence.failure: Stop/destroy are pending until host confirmation; external effects are not reversible.
